unit.sep: Classify by explicit criteria,compare property records,check reaction conditions and separate supplied from observed evidence.
unit.focus: Alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases and transition metals; Physical and chemical properties of selected elements; Uses of the elements and their compounds
unit.phenomenon: A fictional useful-metals poster calls all metals transition elements andequates printed reaction equations with actual investigations.
unit.supportingPhenomena: First20sort,safe physical-observation option,condition-specific reactionrecords,namedmetal-use cards andfictional road-lighting tender.
unit.drivingQuestion: How are elements suited to their use in day-to-day life?
unit.content: Alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases and transition metals; Physical and chemical properties of selected elements; Uses of the elements and their compounds
unit.coreCompetencies:
Self-efficacy: as the learner carries out activities to investigate the reaction of sodium, magnesium and chlorine with air and dilute acids.
Digital literacy: as the learner uses available digital and print media to research on transition elements and their uses.
unit.values: Love: as the learner takes care of self and others by observing safety when carrying out activities to investigate properties of elements of the periodic table and appropriately using first aid kits in case of injuries.
unit.pcis: Road safety: as the learner discusses with peers the properties of elements that make them suitable for use in illuminating roads.

assessment.instructions: Independent 40 minutes: 5 read CF12, 8 Section1, 8 Section2, 12 Section3, 7 Section4/check/submit. Use only final reference and prompts; no teacher key or answer hints. Actual chemical, digital or first-aid performance is not certified.

sections.title: 1. Families and classification
sections.prompt: Using CF12, classify Li,Ca,Cl,Ne,Cu,Pb into the five named families or an appropriate other category. Correct the claims that all group1 elements are alkali metals and that Pb is transition; give reasons.
sections.exemplar: Li alkali; Ca alkaline earth; Cl halogen; Ne noble; Cu transition; Pb other,group14 p-block. Hydrogen is in group1 but is not an alkali metal. Metallic appearance does not establish the incomplete-d criterion; Pb is not transition.

sections.title: 2. Properties,uses and investigation evidence
sections.prompt: Explain a suitable use of M and N from their supplied properties; name an important limit for each. Explain why the reference conductivity test does not establish that learners investigated chemical properties. State one observation that a safe,approved physical investigation could collect,and label it planned rather than performed.
sections.exemplar: M is conducting Cu,so wiring is supported with appropriate electrical installation controls. N is relatively unreactive Ar,which supports shielding,but does not mean safe to breathe. A supplied low-voltage reference test is physical data,not actual student chemical performance. A planned approved Cu appearance/conductivity comparison could collect physical observations; no actual test is claimed.

sections.title: 3. Equations and applicable evidence
sections.prompt: Balance both CF12 records and give all atom counts. Explain the reversible arrow and why chlorine need not undergo every possible listed combination. Reject the proposed learner chlorine/oxygen/acid tests,and explain how this written work differs from an actual chemical investigation.
sections.exemplar: Mg+2HCl→MgCl2+H2 has Mg1,Cl2,H2 on each side. Cl2+H2O⇌HCl+HClO has Cl2,H2,O1 on each side; both directions are possible. Where applicable requires valid chemistry and conditions,not every combination. No learner chlorine/acid handling or forced ordinary oxygen reaction is supported. A written balance does not prove an actual reaction or performance.

sections.title: 4. Daily use and road-safety conclusion
sections.prompt: Explain a property-to-use link for sodium lighting. State two further road-safety/evaluation criteria and the evidence needed. Explain why the given facts cannot prove sodium lighting is cheapest or best,and state one way accurate element knowledge helps daily decisions.
sections.exemplar: Excited sodium vapour has characteristic yellow-orange emission used in lamps. Glare,visibility,colour discrimination,maintenance and reliability need site evidence; energy and cost also require actual data. Colour alone does not determine the best choice. Accurate property knowledge helps choose materials under appropriate conditions and limits.

rubric.excellent: All placements and exceptions correct with definition-based Pb/H reasons.
rubric.proficient: Most placements correct with a valid criterion.
rubric.developing: Some family knowledge,but forces other members or confuses definitions.

rubric.excellent: Both specific links and limits correct; physical,supplied,planned and chemical-performance distinctions clear.
rubric.proficient: Valid links and a principal evidence limit.
rubric.developing: One use plausible,but property or performance distinction incomplete.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs support to connect property,use and evidence.

rubric.excellent: Both records balanced with full tallies; equilibrium,applicability and safety limits accurate.
rubric.proficient: Correct balances with valid condition and safety limits.
rubric.developing: Partial balance or condition reasoning; some unsupported claims.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided atom counts and recognition of inapplicable work.

rubric.excellent: Specific emission link,two evidence criteria and precise decision limit.
rubric.developing: Names a use but misses conditions or makes an unsupported best-choice claim.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs prompts to connect properties with daily evidence.
